text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. ALL NEWSPAPERS

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said at Okayama in Japan that there was a political agenda behind the recent speculative attacks on Southeast Asian currencies. He said an American financier opposed to a move to admit Burma into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) grouping was behind the attack on currencies.
-- ASEAN will adopt Vision 2020, a programme of achieving peace, freedom, prosperity and neutrality, at the Summit of its leaders in December.

-- Ekran Bhd and ABB Asea Brown Boveri will meet on Thursday to resolve a dispute over major terms of a contract to build the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric power project, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said. Ekran Bhd which was awarded the project, has handed a $5.5 billion contract to ABB to construct the dam.
-- Malaysia remains committed to achieving a surplus budget by keeping a tight rein on spending, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said at a dialogue with industry in Malacca.

-- Cambodia is considering compensation for foreign firms affected by violent clashes between rival factions in the government, second Prime Minister Hun Sen said in a televised address. Hun Sen has ousted first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh in a bloody battle two weeks ago, taking the country to the brink of civil war. Hun Sen estimated total damages to foreign property in the region of $10 million.

-- The U.S. petrochemicals giant, Dupont will set up manufacturing facilities in Malaysia involving "several hundred million ringgit per project", the company's manager in Malaysia Hapiz Abdullah said.
-- The Economic Advisor to the Malaysian government Daim Zainuddin said the ringgit's relative weakness will not last long and said the fall in the currency's value was a boon to exporters.
-- Metroplex Bhd is planning to invest $10 million in a South African casino.
